notes: Linux only: on Windows Go itself skips these two through the same MustHaveDebugOptionsSupport guard, so both runtimes skip identically there and the Windows row stays 8 matched / 0 disclosed; this entry fires only where Go's side runs them.

disclosures.name: TestDisableAllCapabilities
disclosures.signature: skipping test: cpu feature options not supported by OS
disclosures.reason: Capability-detection divergence (board class W6, coordinator-ruled platform-skip 2026-08-27 at the Linux bank, roster commit 030f9e783). Go on Linux re-executes the test binary with GODEBUG=cpu.all=off and checks that internal/cpu reports every feature disabled; the converted host takes Go's OWN skip branch, MustHaveDebugOptionsSupport, because the managed runtime does not expose the x86 capability-disable options the GODEBUG path drives, and skips with that upstream text. Nothing go2cs owns can satisfy the assertion without emulating cpuid feature masking inside the CLR. The bank captured the signature from the run but committed the roster line only; this manifest is that bank's missing artifact, added 2026-09-03 when the Linux leveling re-sweep at 22d2bd9dc read the row 6 matched + 2 unabsorbed and the roster guard gained the line that every disclosed count must be backed by a committed manifest.

disclosures.name: TestDisableSSE3
disclosures.signature: skipping test: cpu feature options not supported by OS
disclosures.reason: Same mechanism as TestDisableAllCapabilities with GODEBUG=cpu.sse3=off: Go on Linux runs it, the converted host takes MustHaveDebugOptionsSupport's own skip because the managed runtime exposes no per-feature disable, and skips with the upstream text. Board class W6, platform-skip as ruled 2026-08-27; manifest committed 2026-09-03 alongside its sibling entry.
